newsitem.title: FRANCE: Total set to lose shareholder pact defence.
newsitem.headline: Total set to lose shareholder pact defence.

text.p: Total chairman Thierry Desmarest said the group was set to lose its anti-takeover defence next year when a shareholder pact expires but added that a takeover would not be cheap.

"The group of stable shareholders today represents around 18 percent of the capital. When the pact expires in about a year, its representation could decline to 15 percent. A takeover might then be possible but we wouldn't be sold at a bargain," Desmarest told a conference organised by CCF Elysees Bourse.
He reiterated there was no plan to try and get closer to French rival Elf-Aquitaine.
"When we look at the French companies' size, we have the means to increase growth. There's no point creating disruptions and putting at risk our profitability," he said.
